stops.note: 'amber'; Thales of Miletus (c. 600 BC) was said to have noticed that rubbed amber attracts light objects
amber, and also the pale gold-silver alloy of the same colour
William Gilbert, physician to Elizabeth I, coined it in De Magnete (1600) for substances that attract things when rubbed, like amber
Sir Thomas Browne's Pseudodoxia Epidemica (1646) is the first English book to use the word

current_meaning: a form of energy from charged particles, supplied as current
